subject: Subprocessor chain visibility and DPA evidence for CCPA/CPRA request
messages:
From: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@wellcare.org>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Chen <mike.chen@wellcare.org>
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Evidence & mapping for 'service provider' classification under CCPA/CPRA

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week. As part of our legal review for the pilot, our privacy team needs the following so our counsel can confirm Redwood will meet the CPRA/CCPA service provider obligations when we ingest telemetry and model outputs:

1) A current list of subprocessors that handle telemetry or model inference artifacts, with the geographic regions where they process data.
2) A short explanation of how Redwood classifies "service provider" vs. "processor" for US state privacy (we have state-by-state counsel asking for criteria).
3) Evidence that you do not "sell" data under CCPA — specifically whether any non-aggregated telemetry is shared with advertising/monetization partners.
4) A manifest (hashes and timestamps) for a sample telemetry export (schema + example rows) to validate retention & deletion handling.

If possible, can you provide a consolidated packet we can attach to our SOC/contract review? We aim to present it to procurement/legal by Tuesday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Sara

--
Sara Bennett
Director, Privacy & Risk
WellCare Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@wellcare.org>, Mike Chen <mike.chen@wellcare.org>
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Evidence & mapping for 'service provider' classification under CCPA/CPRA

Hi Neha / Laura — looping you in for scope and artifacts. Sara asked for a consolidated "packet" for WellCare legal. Can you confirm what we can share publicly vs. what requires Legal approval?

Quick notes on what I think we can put together immediately:
- Subprocessor list (service roles + region): we have an internal spreadsheet (redwood_dpa_tracker.xlsx) that lists current cloud/infra partners and whether they handle telemetry. Can redact contact emails, but need to confirm onshore/offshore flags.
- Classification statement: short paragraph describing Redwood's default position (we act as a service provider for inbound customer prompt+response telemetry except when customers request processor-level handback or on-prem deployments).
- Telemetry manifest: we can export a sample telemetry CSV and a manifest file with SHA256 hashes (telemetry_export-manifest.txt) for proof-of-handing and TTL.

Legal / Security: please advise on the OK to send the subprocessor map (pdf) and the DPA tracker as attachments to the external recipients. Also confirm whether we should provide a redlined DPA excerpt instead of our full tracker.

4DD Action items:
- Neha: produce subprocessor map PDF and confirm regions + onshore fallback notes.
- Laura: draft the classification paragraph and a short cover note for the packet.
- Marcus: coordinate final packet and send to Sara.

Thanks,
Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@wellcare.org>, Mike Chen <mike.chen@wellcare.org>
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 08:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Evidence & mapping for 'service provider' classification under CCPA/CPRA

Marcus / Laura / Sara — quick update from Security & Legal intake: attaching the subprocessor chain map and the telemetry manifest (attachment stubs below). I redacted vendor contact PII and any internal SLA rates.

Attachments (referenced):
- subprocessor_chain_map.pdf (high-level: lists infra partners, managed services, onboarding processors; flags onshore fallback nodes)
- telemetry_export-manifest.txt (SHA256 hashes + row count sample; no PII included in sample rows)
- redwood_dpa_tracker.xlsx (internal tracker; redacted columns: contract notes and commercial terms)

Summary of classification (draft):
"Redwood Inference acts as a service provider under CCPA/CPRA for hosted API customers by processing customer-provided prompts, generated responses, and transient telemetry on behalf of the customer. Data is only used to provide and improve inference services when explicitly permitted by contract. For customers requiring processor-level handling (jurisdictional restrictions or regulated workloads), Redwood offers Dedicated and Private deployment models with contractual processor commitments and on-prem/VPC deployment options. Subprocessor engagements that involve telemetry processing are documented and subject to: (i) contractual restrictions prohibiting sale of customer data, (ii) onshore fallback/residency commitments where requested in the DPA, and (iii) periodic attestations to customers on request."

Sara — a couple of clarifications we need from you to finalize the packet:
1) Are you asking for a one-time manifest (sample) or periodic attestation cadence (quarterly)?
2) Do you need per-state mapping (CPRA vs. specific state nuances) or a single US-level service-provider statement?

If you confirm the above, I'll finalize the tracker for redaction and send the packet.

-Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Head of Privacy & Security, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@wellcare.org>, Mike Chen <mike.chen@wellcare.org>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Evidence & mapping for 'service provider' classification under CCPA/CPRA

Sara / Mike — attaching the compliance packet we discussed. See notes below and attachments.

Attachment list (sent): redwood_dpa_tracker.xlsx, subprocessor_chain_map.pdf, telemetry_export-manifest.txt

Cover note:
Hi Sara — thanks for the list. Attached is a redacted DPA/subprocessor packet that includes: (1) the current subprocessor roster and processing regions, (2) a short classification paragraph for CCPA/CPRA service-provider treatment, and (3) a sample telemetry manifest with SHA256 hashes showing retention/deletion timestamps. We do not share telemetry with ad or monetization partners — telemetry is used for routing/health/ops and for improving core inference only where customers have explicitly opted in.

Answers to your clarifying Qs:
- Manifest cadence: we can provide a one-time sample manifest now and offer quarterly attestation if you need periodic evidence for audits.
- State mapping: the attached classification paragraph is US-level; if you want per-state nuance (e.g., CPRA vs. proposed state-specific definitions), we can coordinate with your counsel and our legal team to produce a short supplement.

Next steps: let us know if the packet is sufficient for procurement/legal and whether you prefer the quarterly attestation model. Happy to set a short call if helpful.

Best,
Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_dpa_tracker.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), subprocessor_chain_map.pdf (pdf stub), telemetry_export-manifest.txt (text stub)
